Method of Attack: Compromises Redis servers without authentication by issuing 'SLAVEOF' command to synchronize a master server under attacker control
Deploys malware that runs in memory to bypass anti-malware scans
Deletes logs and communicates only with attacker-controlled servers to evade detection
Loads payloads through memfd, memory-only files, and kernel modules loaded directly from memory avoiding disk writes
Uses compromised servers as mining pools to mine Monero cryptocurrency
Discoverer: Aqua Security researchers Nitzan Yaakov and Asaf Eitani
Attack Vector: Exposed Redis servers accessible from outside local network due to lack of authentication and misconfiguration
Indicators of Compromise: Approximately 1,200 actively infected Redis servers detected
Communication with legitimate IP addresses primarily other infected servers
No detections on VirusTotal for analyzed samples
Monero wallet linked to botnet showing estimated annual profit of around $4,500 per worker
